title: Post-shift regression quiver — mini digest
body:
Purpose: quick, post-shift notes capturing a ~20-sample small-batch regression run. Not a formal triage — this is my raw reasoning and hypotheses for follow-ups.

Summary (topline):
- Observed 3 distinct failure signatures across 20 samples after the rw-internal/1.2 rollout on ded-nyc-1.
- Two signatures likely tied to recent KV-cache change (MR 788) + slight prompt-prefix tokenization drift.
- One signature appears unrelated (prompt-anchoring hallucination) — maybe data/regression set skew.

Quick reproduction notes (commands I ran):
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw-internal-1.2","prompt":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":256,"stream":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
- Local runner using --kv-cache=on/quant-path=auto to compare variants.

Failure signatures (examples):
1) Truncated reasoning mid-step (signature: "kv-trunc")
- Sample IDs: 003, 010, 017
- Symptom: response ends abruptly with a mid-sentence stop, final token often a punctuation + newline.
- Minimal repro: long-chain-of-thought prompt + followup question.
- Quick hypothesis: KV cache mis-eviction on cross-request reuse (older tokens incorrectly replaced).
- Heuristic check: re-run with --kv-cache=off -> deterministic long-form output returns.

2) Token misalignment at prompt boundary (signature: "boundary-shift")
- Sample IDs: 005, 012
- Symptom: output repeats the last 1-3 words of the prompt as if shifted; extra tokens inserted before first new sentence.
- Minimal repro: prompt ends with partial word or backtick.
- Hypothesis: tokenizer update (v2.3) + subtle change in how prefix is buffered into KV. Off-by-one in prefix length.
- Quick mitigation: re-tokenize prompt with explicit whitespace or "
" to force clean boundary.

3) Confident hallucination/anchored spite (signature: "anchored-halluc")
- Sample IDs: 002, 011, 019
- Symptom: model confidently fabricates a short code snippet referencing nonexistent API (e.g., Redwood SDK v0.3 method).
- Hypothesis: evaluation prompt includes sample context lines from stale docs; model treats them as ground truth. Not an inference engine bug per se.
- Action: prune eval set and flag prompts that include doc fragments.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric used in this pass (very rough):
- 0: Pass (expected or acceptable variance)
- 1: Minor deviation (rewording, harmless extra tokens)
- 2: Material regression (truncation, wrong order, repeated tokens)
- 3: Critical break (hallucinated facts that would break product behavior)

Annotated sample (one-liners):
- 003: 2 (kv-trunc) — cuts off after step 4 of 6, loses decisive instruction.
- 005: 2 (boundary-shift) — outputs: "...use fetchData()fetchData() then..." (duplicate fragment).
- 011: 3 (anchored-halluc) — invents `redwood.fetch_secret()` and shows an API call.

Quick experiments I ran during the session:
- A/B with kv-cache on vs off (5 samples each): 4/5 problematic samples fixed when kv-cache off.
- Tokenizer normalization: normalizing prompt to NFC + explicit space removed boundary-shift in 1/2 cases.
- Increasing max_tokens by 20 did NOT fix truncation in kv-trunc cases (so not a strict max_token cutoff).

Immediate next steps (short):
- Tag sample IDs 003,010,017 as kv-trunc and move to a separate queue for SRE replay. (Assign to Ethan)
- Run a 100-sample randomized run with kv-cache=off to verify overall delta. (Assign to me, target 1/21)
- Add a small harness test: synthetic long-chain-of-thought prompt -> expect >200 tokens and no abrupt stop. Put in CI as flaky test. (PR idea: add to infra-tests).
- Email draft to runtime team summarizing MR 788 suspicion; include exact sample excerpts. (Assign to Noah to shepherd)

Longer-term thoughts / hypotheses (brain-dump):
- KV caching gains are likely beneficial for latency/cost but we may have an LRU boundary bug when sequence windows vary across requests. Possible thought: cache keys currently depend on (request-id, truncated-prefix-hash) rather than absolute token offsets. If so, overlapping prefixes across sessions could cause eviction anomalies.
- Another angle: quantized kernel (int8 path) introduced a subtle rounding factor that pushes decoder into early STOP token under some logits distributions. Needs logit-level trace.
- Regression triage roadmap: start with isolation (kv off), then binary search in runtime flags (quant path vs float), then tokenizer difference. Keep record of which combination reproduces.

Notes to self (meta):
- Keep this informal. Capture timestamped commands inside the ticket. Avoid over-indexing on 20-sample pass. Want to escalate only if 10%+ of a larger sample set shows same signature.
- Save raw outputs to: s3://redwood-test/quiver-2025-01-18/ (I uploaded current dump).

Misc quick links I used:
- Runtime perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/788
- Tokenizer notes (confluence): /display/INF/tokenizer-v2.3
- KV cache design doc: /display/INF/kv-cache

Action log (who will do what):
- Keiko: run 100-sample kv-cache=off (by 2025-01-21)
- Ethan: SRE replay on ded-nyc-1 with sample IDs (ASAP)
- Noah: draft runtime brief + include three sample excerpts (EOD 2025-01-20)

Unresolved questions: 
- Is this reproducible across regions (ded-sfo-1)? I noticed slightly different failure rates locally vs ded-nyc-1.
- Do we have epoched cache snapshots to compare before/after MR 788?
- If this is quant-path specific, can we get raw logits for a few runs to inspect STOP distribution?

End of pass. Keeping this deliberately terse — will flesh into a proper triage doc if the larger run shows the same signatures.

-- Keiko
